newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Most Cambodians happy with government -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Cambodians happy with government -- poll.

text.p: A majority of Cambodians are happy with the performance of the coalition government and its two prime ministers, according to the results of a poll released on Thursday.

But the independent SODECO (Solidarity and Community Development Association) poll found a greater number believed the ex-communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP) was more trustworthy than its coalition partner, the royalist FUNCINPEC party.

Thirty percent of a survey sample of 1,004 men and women aged from 18 to over 55 said they believed in the CPP and counted on it to solve the country's problems compared with 21.9 percent for FUNCINPEC and just 6.3 percent for the opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP).

Of those questioned in Phnom Penh and the provinces from October 22-28, 56 percent said they were satisfied with the government's performance since its formation in 1993, against 9.9 percent who were disatisfied and 16.8 percent who thought the coalition had done a mediocre job.

Almost half (45.9 percent) of those asked to assess the performances of co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh of FUNCINPEC and CPP's Hun Sen said both had done a fair job while 7.4 percent thought the two men had performed badly.
Ranariddh was picked as the better prime minister by 15.1 percent, just ahead of the 14 percent vote for Hun Sen.

More than half (51.3 percent) said peace was the most pressing task facing the government, followed by poverty (15.7 percent), corruption (14.1 percent), deforestation (4.2 percent), immigration (two percent) and border demarcation (1.5 percent).
SODECO is a non-governmental group set up earlier this year to conduct independent public opinion polls under the guidance of French-trained statisticians. It has close links to the KNP.
